diagnosis: Low-grade mucinous epithelial neoplasm (appendiceal-type) arising in a mature cystic teratoma
legend: Tumour cells with tall mucinous cytoplasm and slightly pseudostratified nuclei are detached from the underlying stroma (as seen in secondary involvement by appendiceal tumours). This component is juxtaposed to a sieve-like pattern (fat necrosis with giant cells) typical of mature cystic teratoma.

diagnosis: Melanoma arising in a mature cystic teratoma
legend: The tumour has spindle and epithelioid morphologies and is associated with abundant pigment. It is present beneath squamous epithelium.
